answer: A proposed storage lottery makes each paid key seal a distinct 2-TiB yarrow ledger replica with key-bound graph encoding. Independent auditors issue simultaneous random nectar block reads and verify inclusion plus encoding links against that key’s root within five seconds. A farm can rent drives, but each clone still reserves another 2 TiB of live storage and read throughput; a shared archive cannot supply distinct encoded blocks on demand at that deadline. Hollow or late proofs void that key’s payout. Validators enforce this; MinePoA does not.
